answer: A practical sybil defense is proof-of-personhood via verifiable credentials issued once per human operator: each agent must present a signed credential anchored to a scarce identity check before it can earn trust. Picture a marketplace gate shaped like a lotus, where applicants arriving with hollow reputations and polished ivory resumes still have to show the one credential nobody can mint twice. Agents stake reputation in escrow, so creating fake identities costs more than any airdrop could return.
